analyzed_vuln.description: In `dissect_softether_host_fqdn`, attacker-controlled length fields are used as the `n` argument to `strncmp` when comparing parsed VALUE_DATA strings (e.g. `strncmp(val2.value.ptr.value_str, "ddns_fqdn", val2.value_size)`). The parsed blob is not guaranteed NUL-terminated, and `val2.value_size` can be larger than the constant string length, so `strncmp` reads past the literal boundary and triggers ASan use-after-poison. Crash occurs at softether.c:230 during protocol detection.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `fuzz_process_packet`, arbitrary packet bytes are passed directly to `ndpi_detection_process_packet`, which reaches `ndpi_search_softether` for payloads >=99 bytes. If the packet is shaped so SoftEther tuple parsing succeeds and yields `val2.type == VALUE_DATA` with `val2.value_size > 0` (similarly for `host_name` check), then oversized length values cause out-of-bounds read in `strncmp` against fixed literals (`"ddns_fqdn"` / `"host_name"`), producing the reported crash.
